title: Valid Excel cells without explicit references are silently ignored
reasoning: SpreadsheetML cell references are commonly present but optional. When a producer omits c@r, the adapter skips the cell entirely instead of inferring its address from row and cell order, losing worksheet data from otherwise valid .xlsx files.
reproduction: A worksheet row like <row r="1"><c><v>10</v></c><c><v>20</v></c></row> should map to A1 and B1, but parseWorksheet continues before reading either value.
recommendation: Track the current row number and column index while walking sheetData, infer missing refs, and advance the column cursor from explicit refs when present.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The spreadsheet fixtures exercise standard generated cells with explicit refs; no test removes c@r to cover the optional-reference path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an xlsx fixture whose worksheet has one or more <c> elements without r attributes and assert inferred A1/B1 references are present.
minimumFixScope: Update parseWorksheet address handling and add one adapter-level Excel test.
